server.note: voxel-web.mjs also performs the export when run without --no-export, so the URL is reproducible with one command.

environment.webgl_renderer: ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) UHD Graphics (0x00009B41) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)

build.source_unchanged: No tracked .gd source was modified for the web export; index.pck differs from the Phase 18 game build only because it packs this project's own resources.

windows_exe_unchanged.note: Adding the Web preset did not rebuild or alter the native Windows export.

page.title: voxel-sandbox
page.note: The canvas is one CSS pixel smaller than its backing store because this host reports devicePixelRatio 1.0000000149; the page screenshot is taken at scale 'device', so the PNGs are 1290x800.

console.only_error: The root document of this element is not valid for pointer lock.
console.explanation: The scene requests MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED in _ready(); browsers refuse pointer lock without a user gesture, so the request fails once per page load. Clicking the canvas recaptures the mouse and play continues. No game code error occurred.

network.wasm_sniffing_note: application/wasm is required for WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming; the helper sets it explicitly.

input.method: Playwright Chromium through the browser MCP. The canvas was clicked once to focus and acquire pointer lock; that click is not counted as a game action. Keys were held across many rendered frames. Each observation below was read from the HUD text inside the named screenshot, and the screenshots were pixel-diffed against each other.

observations.action: open the URL and wait for the first rendered frame
observations.observed: Terrain, sky, crosshair, hotbar and the full HUD render; the player stands on the spawn column.

observations.action: one left click on the canvas
observations.observed: Exactly one block was removed and exactly one inventory unit was added; the feedback line names the removed cell.
The player advanced 3.5 m along the view direction and stayed grounded.

observations.action: press Space and capture 170 ms later
observations.observed: Y rose from 4.0 to 5.2 and the grounded flag flipped to no while airborne.
The game handled F5 itself and wrote the save; the browser did not reload the page.

observations.action: click the canvas, then press F9
observations.observed: The saved world and player state were read back through browser IndexedDB; the changed-block count matched the saved state.

clip.method: Captured as a PNG sequence through the browser page-screenshot API at roughly 8 frames per second while scripted input ran (walk, strafe, jump, mine, F5), then encoded with ffmpeg -framerate 8. It is not a desktop screen recording.
clip.fidelity_check: All 58 decoded frames were compared against the source PNGs: mean absolute channel error 1.73, p99 15, which is h264 quantisation only.
clip.not_a_benchmark: Frame pacing is limited by screenshot round-trips, so the clip is not evidence of frame rate or smoothness.

limits: Real browser chrome shortcuts cannot be exercised from an automation harness. F5/F9 were delivered as page key events and the game consumed them (the save and load feedback lines prove it), but 'does F5 reload a real user's tab?' is unverified; the exported index.js contains no F5/F12 special-casing, so a reload is expected to behave like any page reload.
The pointer-lock request in _ready() fails on every load until the user clicks; that console error is expected, not a defect.
Saves live in browser IndexedDB (user:// maps to the web filesystem), so they are per-origin and are cleared by site-data removal.
Verified on one Windows host with Intel UHD graphics only; not tested on another GPU, another browser engine, or a clean VM.
Scripted input is not human input. The clip and screenshots show the game reacting to synthetic key and mouse events.

While collecting this evidence, several capture paths on this host produced torn or tiled frames: Playwright's page screenshots above roughly 1280 px, ffmpeg gdigrab/ddagrab desktop capture, and the conversation image viewer all did so at different times. Each shipped PNG was therefore checked numerically at 1:1, and the shipped clip was checked frame-by-frame against its source PNGs. Earlier discarded attempts are described in docs/phase19/REPORT.md rather than kept as evidence.
